title: Product Profile: Coffee
subtitle: 2025 Edition
org: Kenya Export Promotion and Branding Agency
intro: Kenya's coffee value chain is one of the country's most important economic assets. Coffee is a leading export earner and supports the livelihoods of more than 700,000 smallholder farmers and their families. Kenyan coffee, grown mainly on small farms in the highlands, is highly regarded in international markets for its bright acidity, full body and distinctive fruity and floral notes. The industry also benefits from an established auction system that rewards quality and from long-running relationships with roasters and traders in Europe, Asia and the Americas.

This profile examines Kenya's trade in coffee (HS 0901 - coffee, whether or not roasted or decaffeinated; coffee husks and skins; coffee substitutes containing coffee), based on trade values reported to the International Trade Centre (ITC). The analysis covers the period 2016 to 2025.

Only product headings that relate to coffee are included in this profile; other headings under the spices section, such as tea and mate, are excluded to keep the analysis focused on the coffee value chain.

recommendations: Deepen market presence in premium, specialty-coffee destinations that reward Kenyan arabica quality.
Strengthen cupping and certification programmes to maintain Kenya's price premium relative to competing origins.
Expand manufacturing of roasted and value-added coffee to capture higher unit values than green-bean exports.
